Cartaginés|Cartaginés]] |longest wins = |longest unbeaten = |longest losses = |highest attendance = |lowest attendance = |average attendance = |prevseason = [[2010–11 Costa Rican Primera División season|2010–11]] |nextseason = [[2012–13 Costa Rican Primera División season|2012–13]] }} The '''2011–12 Primera División season''' is the 93rd of [[Costa Rica]]'s top-flight professional [[association football|football]] league. The season was divided into two championships: the [[#Campeonato de Invierno|Invierno]] and the [[#Campeonato de Verano|Verano]]. The season began on 31 July 2011. == Promotion and relegation == [[Club de Futbol Universidad de Costa Rica|Universidad de Costa Rica]] finished [[2010–11 Costa Rican Primera División season|last season]] in last place in the overall table at the end of last season and were relegated to the [[Segunda División de Costa Rica|Segunda División]]. Replacing them in the league for this season are the overall champions of last season's Segunda División competition, [[A.D. Belén|Belén Siglo XXI]]. [[Club de Fútbol Barrio México|Barrio México]] were expelled from last year's competition during the 2011 Verano tournament and were eventually relegated from the league due to various financial difficulties.{{cite web|last=Herrera|first=Juan José|title=Asamblea de la Unafut expulsó a Barrio México|url=http://www.nacion.com/2011-03-02/Deportes/NotaPrincipal/Deportes2700719.aspx|publisher=La Nación|accessdate=28 June 2011| archiveurl= https://web.archive.org/web/20110714150052/http://www.nacion.com/2011-03-02/Deportes/NotaPrincipal/Deportes2700719.aspx| archivedate= 14 July 2011 | url-status= live}} They were not replaced for this season. For this season, [[Brujas F.C.|Brujas]] changed their name to ''Orión FC Desamparados''.{{cite web|title=Orión FC Desamparados|url=http://unafut.com/site/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=1317%3Abrujas&catid=2&Itemid=2|publisher=UNAFUT|accessdate=23 July 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110712092943/http://www.unafut.com/site/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=1317:brujas&catid=2&Itemid=2|archive-date=12 July 2011|url-status=dead}} == Format changes == Due to the reduction of the league to 11 teams for this season, the league's format was changed for this season. There would be no groups this season. Instead, for both tournaments, the clubs would play every other club twice, once at home and once away, for a total of 20 matches each. At the end of the regular season, the top 4 teams in the league standings would participate in the playoffs. At the end of the season, the last place club would participate in a promotion-relegation playoff against the Segunda División overall runners-up, while the Segunda División overall champions would be promoted to next season's competition automatically.{{cite web|last=Molina Salas|first=José Pablo|title=Asamblea de Unafut acordó cambios en el formato de los próximos torneos|url=http://unafut.com/site/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=1244:asamblea-de-unafut-acordo-cambios-en-el-formato-de-los-proximos-torneos&catid=6:noticias&Itemid=40|publisher=UNAFUT|accessdate=28 June 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111006234758/http://unafut.com/site/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=1244:asamblea-de-unafut-acordo-cambios-en-el-formato-de-los-proximos-torneos&catid=6:noticias&Itemid=40|archive-date=6 October 2011|url-status=dead}} ==Average attendance== *[[Saprissa]] 14,990 *[[Alajuelense]] 9,720 *[[Herediano]] 4,064 *[[Limón]] 3,220 *[[C.S.
